overview: White develops the bishop to g2 instead of the usual Bb5 or Bc4, keeping the centre flexible and avoiding main-line theory. Black can play ...d5 to strike at e4 or settle for ...Nf6 and ...Bc5. The game is a quiet King's Indian-Attack-style fight where White pressures d5 and e5 from a fianchetto and Black is usually comfortable.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto the king's bishop and play d3, O-O and Nc3 for a flexible pressure game.
Meet ...d5 with exd5 and Bg2 or d3 to keep pressure on the long diagonal.

black_ideas.idea: Strike at once with ...d5 to take the centre and force White to react.
Develop ...Nf6, ...Bc5 and castle, with ...d6 and ...Be6 for a solid game.

typical_structures.structure: Open Game with White's bishop on g2 and flexible pawn tension on e4/d3.

character.notes: Quiet, slow play with no forcing lines, neither side forced into risk.

structure.notes: Centre tension between e4 and e5 not yet resolved; flank fianchetto.

level.notes: Easy ideas but gives Black no problems; modest.

character.reason: Quiet development with no forcing play.

level.reason: Simple ideas, not a first repertoire move.

plans.reason: White's Bg2 on the long diagonal.
